rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before data; synthetic validation on real call grids (3 units x 6 worlds) with a dated pre-data amendment (world grid, collapse statistic); replication on 67 units / 34 periods; 3 natives with dated predictions; labelled post hoc fast/slow decomposition; confirm.py frozen, guarded and dry-run. Missing: collapse and late-booter tests (untestable at day resolution), two-timescale synthetic, holdout.
rationale.faithfulness: The registered mean-field relation fails in regime III (K 22 [6.9, 71]) and agrees trivially in regimes I-II because tau0 sits at the one-call floor. Post hoc, the fast part of the boot relaxes within x2 of the call-clock prediction, but the coupling moves the prediction by at most x1.4, so the boot cannot test g_lag. Scorecard A1 B1 C0 D1 E0 F1 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A measurement-hygiene rule: drop the first call of each agent-day in chat-mode scaffolds and treat the first hours of a regime-III day as non-stationary (+10-20% talk). Not a lever and not a coupling gauge.

one_line: The daily boot is a one-call talk spike plus a slow regime-III talk excess; the HH's single-exponential tau = tau0/(1-g_lag) fails in regime III (K_boot 22 [6.9, 71]).

models.note: Single-exponential mean-field Glauber relaxation fails in regime III
Discrete per-call AR form; fits the fast part only

v2.claim: The daily boot is a first-call talk spike that relaxes within about one call (regime I excess 0.36, τ ≈ 0.5–1 call), plus a slow day-scale talk excess in regime III (+12% [4, 20]%); the single-exponential relation τ = τ₀/(1 − g_lag) fails in regime III (K_boot 22 [6.9, 71])
v2.scope: 67 units, 3,135 boots; natives NE14, NE43, NE42
v2.decision: each day's start is a one-call burst, not a slow relaxation the coupling sets
